title: Add hot-route burst + retry-storm scenarios; gate merges on p95/p99 + error budget regression
author: Connor O'Brien
release_notes:
- Adds two new perf-canary scenarios: hot_route_burst and retry_storm_overload
- Introduces merge-gating check that fails PRs when p95/p99 latency or availability burn-rate regress vs baseline
body:
Context: As part of Hot-route capacity protection (ENG-4829), we need perf-canary coverage that reproduces the failure modes we actually see in incidents: (1) sudden bursty load on a small number of hot enterprise routes and (2) retry storms where clients amplify overload with tight retry loops. This PR adds two new scenarios and makes them required in CI for the perf-canary workflow used as a merge gate for control-plane/routing changes.

What’s in this PR: 1) New scenario: hot_route_burst - Targets a configurable set of routes (default: /v1/chat/completions and /v1/embeddings) with an enterprise-style token distribution (longer prompts, higher decode) - Ramps from steady-state to burst (configurable burst_factor, default 3.0x) over 60s, holds for 4m, then recovers - Records p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency, TTFT p95, success rate, and 429/503 rates

2) New scenario: retry_storm_overload - Generates a baseline request stream, then injects a controlled overload window that triggers 429/503s - A retry engine simulates client behavior: exponential backoff with jitter by default; also includes a “bad client” mode (fixed 250ms retry) for incident replay - Tracks amplification factor (total attempts / original requests), and ensures retries do not hide latency regressions

3) Merge gating on p95/p99 and error budget regression - Adds a required GitHub check (perf-canary/hot-route-regression) that compares scenario metrics against an approved baseline stored in-repo - Fails the check if p95 or p99 latency regresses > 7% (configurable) or if availability burn-rate indicates faster error budget consumption during the overload window - The check is designed to be stable: it uses medians across 3 runs, and ignores the first 30s warmup

Operational notes: - These scenarios are intended to run against the staging perf environment (perf-stg) with the “hot-route protection” feature flags disabled by default (to catch raw regressions). A follow-up will add a second job that runs with protections enabled to validate shedding behavior.

Rollout: - This PR initially marks the new check as required only for perf-canary PRs. Once stable for a week, SRE will recommend enabling it as a required check in the redwood monorepo for hot-route related directories.

Test plan: - Ran both scenarios 5x against perf-stg; confirmed variability within thresholds - Verified a forced regression (added 150ms server-side delay) fails p95/p99 gate - Verified a forced error spike (inject 3% 503s) trips burn-rate gate

Notes/limitations: - The burn-rate computation is approximate (windowed) and intentionally conservative to avoid false negatives; we can tune once SLO-toolkit integration lands for per-route/per-tier SLOs.

Owners: - Connor O’Brien (perf-canary) - Rafael Mendes / Sean Gallagher (SRE validation)

Refs: ENG-4829 (load test plan), ENG-4821 (program umbrella), incident notes in #incidents and #eng-oncall (retry storm behavior).
commits: scenario: add hot_route_burst load profile + metrics sinks
scenario: add retry_storm_overload with configurable retry policy + amplification tracking
ci: add hot-route regression gate (p95/p99 + burn-rate) and make check required for this repo
docs: update scenarios README + baseline approval workflow
chore: refactor metrics query helpers + stabilize warmup handling
review_conversation:
Rafael Mendes: Can we avoid paging ourselves with flaky gating? What’s the stability strategy here? Connor O’Brien: Added median-of-3 runs, explicit warmup ignore window, and widened thresholds to 7% for p95/p99 to start. Also made the gate compare against a rolling baseline that requires approval to update.

Aisha Bello: Burn-rate math—what exact signal are we using? Connor O’Brien: Using availability as (successes / total attempts) excluding client-side timeouts; burn-rate approximated as (1 - availability) / (1 - target). This matches how SRE has been reasoning about overload windows, but happy to adjust once per-route SLO objects are wired in.

Mina Haddad: Retry-storm “bad client” mode is scary—do we ever run it on shared staging? Connor O’Brien: It’s off by default and requires RETRY_POLICY=bad_client; CI never sets it. The default is exp-backoff+jitter aligned to our docs.

Sean Gallagher: Please add a clear failure output so engineers know what to do when the gate fails. Connor O’Brien: Done—gate now prints top regressed metrics, baseline vs current, and links to docs/baselines.md with the ‘how to re-run’ commands.

Final approvals: Rafael Mendes approved after threshold tuning + improved output. Sean Gallagher approved after adding warmup ignore and stabilizing the query window.
